title: Validate native iOS/Android STT for meditation use
description:
Pilot `SFSpeechRecognizer` (iOS) and Android `SpeechRecognizer` via a Capacitor plugin to confirm they handle meditation-specific speech patterns before committing to the no-Whisper-on-mobile strategy.

Test cases that may break native APIs (which are tuned for Siri-style queries):
- **Long pauses** without the recognizer giving up / cutting off
- **Soft, whispered, or quiet speech** (relevant during deep meditation)
- **Brief 1–2 word noting utterances** ('warmth', 'tightness', 'sound')
- **Half-finished sentences** trailing into pauses
- **iOS aggressive silence cutoff** — defaults to ~1.5s. Configurable?

Deliverable: a quick prototype Capacitor app or test page that runs the speech recognizer with realistic meditation input. Decision output: do we go native, or do we need a cloud-Whisper fallback path for mobile?

If native fails: streaming audio to a hosted Whisper endpoint is still cheaper than bundling the model. Document the fallback architecture if needed.

title: Stripe direct-purchase path not idempotent (webhook retry double-credits)
description:
routes/billing.ts webhook → ledger.purchase() → ledger.append → sqlite-store.appendEntry INSERTs a row with a random UUID id and NO uniqueness on reason. Stripe retries webhooks, so a duplicate checkout.session.completed delivery on the NON-GIFT path double-credits the account. The gift path is safe only because gifts.stripe_session_id is UNIQUE.

FIX (also unblocks x402 idempotency — see du9 / dev-docs/x402-plan.md step 3):
- Add partial unique index in sqlite-store.ts SCHEMA: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ledger_purchase_ref ON ledger(reason) WHERE kind='purchase';
- appendEntry: on UNIQUE/constraint violation for a 'purchase'-kind entry, treat as idempotent no-op (mirror createGift's catch). Other kinds keep throwing.
- Stripe reason is already purchase:${packId}:${sessionId} (good dedup key). x402 will use purchase:${packId}:x402:${txHash}.
- Add store-parity test: two purchase appends, same reason → one row, credited once.

Discovered while planning du9 (x402). Low risk at current test-mode scale but a real correctness bug before real money flows.
close_reason: Fixed: partial unique index idx_ledger_purchase_ref on ledger(reason) WHERE kind='purchase' + idempotent appendEntry catch in both stores. Covers Stripe AND x402 purchase paths. Tested (store-parity: replayed purchase credits once; non-purchase same-reason entries unaffected). Commit 02d158a.

title: Phase 3A: Modularize session.js
Split signup from identity-connection; gate free credits on a connected OAuth identity (unique per account)
description:
Economics concern (dev, 2026-06-01): we currently grant free credits on signup (decideSignupGrant in server/src/quota/freetier.ts → ledger.grant on first POST /cloud/v1/auth/google, default ALOUD_FREE_SIGNUP_CREDITS=20). With more/easier sign-in methods coming (email — see meditation-pal-s75), 'free credits per new account' is too cheap to farm.

Redesign: decouple SIGN UP from CONNECTING AN IDENTITY.
- Signing up (e.g. with an email/password account) creates an aloud account but grants NO free credits.
- Free credits unlock only when the account CONNECTS a trusted OAuth identity (Google / Apple / maybe others) — something at least a little trouble to mint at scale.
- Each external identity may be connected to AT MOST ONE aloud account, ever (uniqueness on the provider 'sub'/identity, enforced even after disconnect), so re-connecting the same Google/Apple account to a fresh aloud account can't re-trigger the grant. One grant per unique identity, and the grant is per-aloud-account-lifetime.

Implementation notes / open questions:
- Data model: accounts ↔ identities is currently 1:1 (accounts keyed by googleSub). Move to an account with N linked identities (provider + sub, unique index on (provider, sub)). The signup grant moves from 'account created' to 'first eligible identity linked, if account never granted before'.
- The grant decision (freetier.decideSignupGrant) becomes a connect-time check: identity provider is trusted AND email verified AND this identity has never granted AND this account has never been granted.
- Keep the FreeGrantBreaker global hourly cap (freetier.ts) as the backstop.
- Interplay with meditation-pal-cap (hosted abuse/cost controls): that ticket argued federated sign-in is a weak limiter because Google accounts are free to mint — this design treats identity-connection as a *modest* friction + a strict one-grant-per-identity uniqueness rule, NOT as the whole boundary (the daily systemwide budget cap remains the hard backstop). Cross-reference cap.
- UX: a signed-up-but-not-connected user sees a clear 'Connect Google/Apple to claim your free credits' affordance; settings Account section reflects connected identities.

Depends on the account/identity model from meditation-pal-s75 (multi-method sign-in).

comments.author: akrusz

Free grant moved from account-creation to CONNECTING a trusted+verified identity (Google/Apple): once per account, once per identity (decideConnectGrant in quota/freetier.ts, applied in auth/identity.connectIdentity). Email signup is untrusted → account but 0 credits until it connects Google/Apple; connecting while signed in LINKS (bearer) and can't relink an identity bound elsewhere (IdentityConflictError). SQLite migration backfills google_sub → 'google' identity (granted flag from ledger history) and drops the column; idempotent. description:

If not, add an explicit save — listen for WindowEvent::CloseRequested / Destroyed (or RunEvent) and call app.save_window_state(StateFlags::all()), and/or save on Moved/Resized.

title: Remove CLI mode (src/__main__.py, src/main.py)
Mic goes deaf while facilitator is processing/speaking — user speech dropped
description:
Symptom (hands-on, ts-core): while the facilitator is thinking (LLM) or its TTS is playing, the user's speech isn't captured. The mic meter ring still glows (it taps the raw MediaStream), so it LOOKS live, but the input is dropped — confirmed by the user.

Root cause: the listen loop (ui/src/views/session.ts listenLoop) pauses between turns — it only runs ONE stt.start() utterance, then blocks on `busy` (LLM call + await ttsDone) before re-arming. WhisperPcmSttEngine (ui/src/adapters/whisper-pcm-stt.ts, formerly CloudWhisperSttEngine) keeps its audio graph + callback running continuously, but while `capturing=false` the frames go ONLY to the 2s onset pre-buffer ring + barge-in detector, never into `chunks` for transcription. Barge-in only fires on louder speech (0.03 energy gate, to avoid tripping on TTS echo) and, when it fires, just cancels TTS + setHolding(false) — capture doesn't actually resume until the listen loop's next stt.start() after busy clears. So any speech during the processing/TTS window beyond what the 2s pre-buffer holds is lost.

Proposed approaches (need hands-on testing — echo is the hazard):
1. Full-duplex / continuous capture: keep accumulating user audio into chunks even while busy, segment by VAD, submit when an utterance completes. Relies on echoCancellation to keep the facilitator's TTS out. Fullest fix, highest echo risk.
2. Barge-in -> immediate capture: when barge-in fires, cancel TTS AND immediately begin an stt capture session (seeded from the pre-buffer) instead of waiting for busy/ttsDone. Targeted, smaller blast radius. Recommended first step.
3. Partial mitigations: lengthen PRE_BUFFER_MS, lower BARGE_IN_THRESHOLD (false-trip risk on echo).

Surfaced during k1yc verification (2026-06-07) alongside the [HOLD]-speaks-acknowledgment + short-utterance fixes.

comments.author: akrusz
comments.text:
Implemented continuous capture for the engine-driven (server-Whisper / on-device + aloud cloud) path; web-speech/capacitor unchanged (their recognizers can't reject TTS echo). Pending hands-on echo + interruption testing before close.

Changes:
- whisper-pcm-stt.ts: barge-in detection (3-chunk @ 0.03 gate) now runs DURING capture too, not just between turns — so a barge-in is caught while the mic is armed.
- streaming-tts.ts: two abort signals — signal (full: stop generating + speaking, for supersession) and ttsSignal (hush TTS but keep generating, so a barge-in keeps the reply in the transcript).
- session.ts: listenLoop no longer pauses on busy for continuousCapture (= engineDrivenBargeIn); dispatches respondTo fire-and-forget so the mic keeps capturing through the response. respondTo is now interruptible via a turn-generation counter (turnGen) + activeFullAbort/activeTtsAbort; a superseded turn bails without recording; only the latest turn clears busy. Barge-in handler gated on busy so it doesn't clear a silence hold. endSession aborts the in-flight turn.

Risks to watch in testing: TTS echo above the 0.015 VAD gate could capture the facilitator as a false utterance; rapid interruptions stacking respondTo (bounded by gen-supersession). Unit tests added for both abort signals (streaming-tts.test.ts).

comments.author: akrusz
comments.text:
Added per-device echo calibration to de-risk the echo false-trigger (the main hardware-variable risk). While the facilitator's audio is actually playing AND the user is silent, the captured energy IS that device's echo floor — measured live as a slow EMA (echoFloor, seeded at 0.005) and used to lift the VAD speechStarted + barge-in gates above it DURING playback only. Good EC -> gate stays at the static 0.015/0.03 (soft speech still caught); weak EC -> gate rises (capped at ECHO_GATE_MAX=0.035, safely under real speech ~0.04). noiseFloor is kept echo-free (only calibrated during true silence).

Signal: session's tts wrapper brackets actual speak() calls (ttsSpeakingDepth) -> whisperEngine.setTtsActive(true/false), so the gate lifts only while audio plays, not during the silent 'thinking' phase (where interruptions must still register at the normal threshold).

Knobs to tune on real hardware (whisper-pcm-stt.ts): ECHO_EMA_ALPHA=0.05, ECHO_GATE_MARGIN=2.0, ECHO_GATE_MAX=0.035. A future refinement could also measure the user's own speech level to set the cap adaptively rather than assuming ~0.04.

title: Post-parity: decouple TS UI from the wholesale Flask stylesheet @import
description:
The TS UI gets its visual identity by @import-ing the entire Flask stylesheet (src/web/static/css/style.css, ~91KB) into ts/ui/src/style.css, and by reusing Flask's class names verbatim (.participant-*, .session-item, .voice-modal-*, .stepper, etc.). This was the RIGHT call during the migration — it's why parity has been fast and cheap — but once the TS app is the source of truth (esp. if/when the Flask desktop app is deprecated), revisit it.

Downsides to clean up at that point:
- Dead weight: the TS bundle ships the whole Flask sheet incl. rules for things the TS app doesn't use or does differently (pywebview/desktop-only chrome, update banner, tour, etc.). ~12KB gzipped, not huge, but not minimal.
- Coupling both ways: editing Flask CSS silently changes the TS app (we hit this with the orb z-index, breathe keyframes, about-modal). Good while shared; a liability once they diverge.
- Class-name coupling: TS markup depends on Flask's exact class names; a Flask refactor would break TS.
- Build coupling: vite imports CSS from outside ui/ (../../../src/web/static), tying the build to the Flask tree layout.
- No design tokens of our own: TS-only layout used magic numbers (mostly removed now by reusing Flask classes); a tokenized system would be cleaner long-term.

Proposed when at parity: copy the actually-used CSS into ts/ui (or extract a shared package), tree-shake/split it, stop importing the whole sheet, and consider tokenizing. Decide based on whether Flask stays (keep shared) or is retired (TS owns CSS). Relates to meditation-pal-1au (CSS-magic-numbers note) and the parity-audit ticket.
notes: REFRAME (2026-05-26): Python/Flask is being removed entirely — the whole app becomes one TS codebase (desktop via Tauri/Capacitor, web, iOS, Android). So this isn't optional cleanup: when src/web/ is deleted, the ts/ui/src/style.css '@import url(../../../src/web/static/css/style.css)' breaks. Relocating that stylesheet into ts/ (TS owns its CSS) becomes a REQUIRED step of the Python-removal work, not a nice-to-have. The two-way-coupling concern is moot (no Flask to share with); the 'TS must own + can trim dead rules' concern is now the whole point.

title: TS parity: per-session usage tracking (LLM tokens split + STT secs + TTS chars) — match Python session-JSON schema
description:
Mirror the Python per-session usage tracking (implemented 2026-05-24) in the TypeScript rewrite, once the TS orchestration core (meditation-pal-2qg) is functional. DO NOT build now — TS isn't runnable, so the code couldn't be exercised and would drift.

The contract is the persisted session-JSON schema (so saved sessions stay cross-compatible between the Python desktop app and the TS web/mobile app). Match exactly what Python now writes:

Per ASSISTANT exchange produced by a completion (omit on user turns and static/fallback messages):
  tokens_in, tokens_out  (ints; required together when present)
  cache_read, cache_creation  (ints; include only when non-zero)

Per-session "usage" block (always present):
  llm_calls            int  — every completion, incl. off-transcript (summary/resume-intent/noting labels)
  llm_tokens_in        int
  llm_tokens_out       int
  llm_cache_read       int
  llm_cache_creation   int
  stt_seconds          float (rounded 2dp) — ALL transcriptions incl. speculative/command (real STT compute)

title: Cache keep-alive for expensive LLMs during silence (Opus)
description:
Anthropic prompt cache TTL is 5 min. Meditation has long silences, so a user who pauses >5 min lets the cache expire; the next real turn then re-pays cacheCreation on the whole transcript (Opus 1.25x input = $6.25/Mtok) AND eats cache-miss latency (slower first token). For Opus with a ~5k-token transcript that's ~$0.03 + a latency spike per expiry — the premium tier is exactly where this bites.

IDEA (from dev): repurpose the existing "are you still there" check-in to also ping the LLM with a no-op turn ("..." / "(silence)") during silence, resetting the 5-min TTL so the cache stays warm and the next real turn is a cheap cache read + fast.

EVALUATE TWO APPROACHES:
(A) Keep-alive pings via the check-in loop. Cost per ping ≈ cacheRead(full history) + tiny input + small output ≈ $0.0025 for 5k Opus history. Cheaper than repeated expiry/recreation when gaps are frequent. Gate to expensive models only (Opus, maybe Sonnet) — pointless for Gemini ($0.01/Mtok cacheRead).
(B) Anthropic 1-hour extended cache TTL — write once at the 1h rate (Opus $10/Mtok vs $6.25 5-min), no pings, survives long silences, no latency spikes. Possibly SIMPLER and better than pings; compare total cost on a realistic silence profile before building (A).

OPEN QUESTIONS / RISKS:
- Billing UX: do keep-alive pings spend the user's credits during silence? Ticking credits while someone sits quietly is optically bad for a meditation app. Options: absorb them (we eat the cost), or frame as net-savings (keep-alive is cheaper than recreation, so the user's NEXT turn is cheaper). Decide before shipping.
- Cap it: stop keep-alive after N pings / after an unanswered "still there?" so we don't ping forever if the user walked away.
- Where it lives: server-side proxy auto-ping vs client-driven via the check-in. The check-in currently sends a CANNED phrase (no LLM call) — this adds an optional real LLM no-op alongside it.
- Latency win is real (warm cache = faster post-pause response), independent of the cost math.

Gate: worth deciding before going fully live (dev). Relates to pricing calibration (rvy/7xl) and the defaults pass (3w3).

comments.author: akrusz
comments.text:
OPTIMAL TTL MATH (the "when to checkpoint to 1-hour cache" question).

Multipliers on base input rate r (model-independent — holds for Opus/Sonnet/Haiku):
  5-min cache write = 1.25r · 1-hour write = 2r · cache read = 0.1r · uncached = 1r.

Within a session the prefix P (tokens) is re-sent every turn: a warm cache reads it at 0.1r·P; a GAP > TTL expires it, so the next turn re-WRITES the whole prefix. Over a session, prefix cost ≈ (#writes)·write_rate·P, where #writes = 1 + (#gaps exceeding the TTL).

Per-write decision (5-min vs 1-hour for the next write), given p = P(next gap > 5 min):
  extra cost of choosing 1h now = (2r − 1.25r)·P = 0.75r·P
  expected saving           = p · (write − read on a re-creation) = p · (1.25r − 0.1r)·P = p·1.15r·P
  ⇒ choose 1-hour when  p·1.15 > 0.75  ⇒  **p > ~0.65**.

CLEAN RESULTS:
- P CANCELS — the breakeven (p>65%) is independent of conversation length. Longer convos matter only because (a) pauses get more likely → p rises, and (b) P is bigger so the absolute $ at stake is larger (worth bothering).
- Whole-session view: 1h beats 5min once you expect even ONE silence >5 min (and none >1h, ~always true intra-session): Cost_1h ≈ 1·2r·P < Cost_5min ≈ (1+G5)·1.25r·P whenever G5 ≥ 1.
- Gate to Opus/Sonnet only — for Gemini the absolute $ is negligible.

ADAPTIVE POLICY (no future knowledge needed), reuses telemetry we already have:
  1. Start writes at 5-min TTL.
  2. usage_events already logs cache_creation vs cache_read per turn — a turn with large cache_creation after a gap = a MISS.
  3. After the first miss (or once a live pause crosses ~4.5 min, or session duration passes a threshold), escalate subsequent writes to 1-hour TTL. This naturally stops wasting 1h writes near session end (no further turns → no escalation).
This is the dev's "1-hour checkpoints for longer conversations," and it's near-optimal. It also subsumes the keep-alive-ping idea: the 1h TTL avoids the silence-billing UX problem (no pings spending credits while the user is quiet) and the cache-miss latency spike. Recommend: build the adaptive 1h-TTL escalation; treat keep-alive pings as a fallback only if a provider lacks a long TTL.

title: NEDERA: safety design — consent framing, resistance protocol, grounding exit, not-a-therapist boundary (BLOCKS build)
description:
Foundational safety work for the NEDERA mode. **This blocks all build issues** — nothing in the mode ships until this is designed and the dev is satisfied. Part of epic meditation-pal-pmxb.

NEDERA deliberately moves people toward activation and emotional release. Bigger duty of care than open meditation, and aloud is **voice-only** (no eye contact / co-regulation that real NEDERA leans on at deep stages — be honest about this limit).

## Deliverables
- **Entry framing / informed consent:** plain-language description of what the process does (moves toward feeling and possible release), not-a-therapist / not-crisis-care boundary, who it's not for right now (acute crisis, active trauma flashbacks), and a crisis-resources pointer.
- **Resistance protocol baked into the prompts:** the framework says honor dissociation, sleepiness, numbing -> **pause and return later, never push.** Define the LLM behavior and detection cues.
- **Grounding / safe-exit path:** a one-tap "I need to stop / ground" affordance that drops the facilitator into a calm grounding script and out of the protocol, reachable from any stage.
- **Crying/release stance:** distinguish healthy (cleansing, self-completing) from unhealthy (endless spiral) per the framework; facilitator witnesses and does NOT push deeper or prolong.
- **Copy review:** must pass the project's copy rules (no em-dashes, no AI-tells, no low-opacity de-emphasis).

## Decisions to surface to the dev
- How gated is entry (warning screen? explicit acknowledge?).
- Hard stop conditions where the facilitator should disengage and point to human help.

title: LLM efficiency: prompt prefix caching for hosted API (quality-neutral cost win)
description:
QUALITY-NEUTRAL cost optimization for the hosted API path. Prefix caching changes how the SAME input is billed/stored on Anthropic's side — it does NOT trim, summarize, or alter any tokens. The model sees identical context and produces identical output; only cost (and slightly, latency) change. The only failure mode is a cache MISS = pay full price that turn = today's behavior. No quality-degradation path exists. (Contrast: context-size reduction DOES change what the model sees — split out to a separate low-priority ticket.)

CONTEXT (measured 2026-05-24): config uses FULL context. A ~35-min, ~33-turn session re-sends the whole transcript every turn: ~76k tokens of history input + ~51k system-prompt input (~1.56k x 33) vs ~2.7k output. Input is ~98% of volume. The system prompt is ALREADY cached (cache_control in src/llm/anthropic.py); the ~76k history is not.

WHO THIS HELPS: hosted API / future paying users only. The dev's own sessions are on the Claude subscription (flat, not per-token — caching saves nothing) or local Gemma (no token bill). So this is a SERVICE-economics lever, not a local-session change.

THE CHANGE (small, bounded): in src/llm/anthropic.py, add a cache breakpoint (cache_control: ephemeral) on the LAST message of the conversation history each turn, so Anthropic caches the full prefix (system + all prior turns). Next turn the prior prefix is a cache-READ at ~10% input price.
Handle: up to 4 breakpoints allowed; 5-min cache TTL (fine — turns are seconds apart); min cacheable prefix ~1024 tokens Sonnet/Opus (~2048 Haiku), met after a few turns; cache WRITE costs 1.25x on the turn created. Keep request prefix byte-stable (history is append-only, so this holds naturally).
Estimated impact: ~76k full-price history input -> mostly cache-reads => roughly 2-3x lower cost on long sessions (hypothetical Opus session ~$1.40 -> ~$0.45). Makes Opus-for-exploration viability much better.

SCOPE: Anthropic API provider first (+ a test asserting the breakpoint is set and a usage-based check). OpenAI/OpenRouter have their own auto-caching (verify, likely no code). Ollama/local + claude_proxy(subscription): N/A.
MINOR (opportunistic): trim redundant retained content (e.g. [HOLD] prefixes) if cheap.

Relates: meditation-pal-vd3 (proxy — where this lives for the service), meditation-pal-8sj (billing math benefits), meditation-pal-14s (cost-meter numbers drop). Latency/context companion: see the split-out local-context ticket.

title: Comms strategy: communicate device capability via runtime detection + honest practice-tiering (no spec tables)
description:
STRATEGY / direction note — draft actual copy LATER (text will change; capture the approach now).

Communicate on-device capability via RUNTIME DETECTION + honest practice-tiering, NEVER device spec tables. Solves cross-platform fragmentation (esp. Android's many manufacturers) by never enumerating devices: read available RAM at first launch, pick the model tier live, and tell the user what THEIR phone can do.

Why: free app => no refund/chargeback exposure on the download, but App Store/Play REVIEWS are the real risk. A static "runs great on your phone" claim is false on 4GB devices (iPhone 13 floor) and earns 1-star "the AI is dumb on my phone" reviews. Honest, detected expectation-setting avoids that.

Three layers, each says a different amount:
1. STORE LISTING — say the least, lead with values; no device-performance claims (can't be conditional, they rot). One honest sentence, e.g.: "aloud runs a private AI on your device, free — nothing leaves your phone. Newer phones run a larger model; on any phone you can connect your own AI key or add hosted sessions for the most in-depth practices." Borrow Apple's "Optimized for newer devices" register. On Play Console: set a real RAM/API-level floor in the device catalog so Play auto-filters phones too weak for even the smallest model (fragmentation backstop done by the store, not by copy).
2. APP FIRST-RUN — where the real honesty lives. Detect RAM/chip, pick tier, say plainly which practices suit it: simpler practices (breath/body/emotions) complete on-device; exploration/parts work "a larger model helps — connect your own key or use hosted." Frame on-device as "private, runs entirely on your phone," NEVER "lite/basic" (a2j crippleware guardrail). Honesty is in WHICH practices each tier is pointed at, not in calling the small model bad.
3. WEBSITE — allowed to be a bit more concrete: one "Will it run on my phone?" section with honest RAM bands + reassurance that the app detects automatically. Still open with practice/values, not a spec table.

Android: read total RAM (ActivityManager.MemoryInfo), bucket into same bands as iOS, load matching model. Same capability vocabulary on both platforms, derived from RAM, never device name.

Vocabulary: give users EXPERIENCE names, never parameter counts (never "1B vs 4B"). E.g. "On-device (private)" -> "Your own key" -> "Hosted (deepest)", with a quiet non-anxious note on the on-device tier about which practices suit it. Pairs with the cost-transparency meter (meditation-pal-14s): radical honesty about both compute spend AND device capability = one coherent trust-building brand.

Correction captured here too: Apple Intelligence Foundation Models require 8GB RAM (iPhone 15 Pro+/16+), so they do NOT reach the iPhone 13 / 4GB floor — must ship our own model (MLC/llama.cpp/Core ML) for that tier. See meditation-pal-dbd (assumption needs fixing) and meditation-pal-0vb (validate the right model per RAM tier).

Touches: meditation-pal-toz (web page), meditation-pal-7rh (store submission), meditation-pal-a2j (honesty/values copy guardrail), meditation-pal-14s (cost meter), meditation-pal-dbd / meditation-pal-0vb (on-device tiering).
notes: 2026-05-27: on-device STT/TTS specifics for the tier picker (from shell-decision review, full detail on meditation-pal-nn1). STT tiers by RAM band: tiny.en (~75MB) -> base.en (~142MB) -> small.en (~180MB quantized, best quality, flagship). TTS: bundle Piper 'mid' voices (~20-60MB each) on all tiers. Models are DOWNLOAD-ON-DEMAND at first run (iOS On-Demand Resources / Android Play Asset Delivery or own CDN), NOT bundled in the store binary — keeps store download small; on-disk footprint ~100-500MB depending on tier, normal for the category. The first-run detect-and-recommend flow is the download decision point: detect RAM/chip -> recommend tier -> download matching model -> ALWAYS let the user opt out to hosted (never force the storage cost). Reinforces the existing experience-name vocabulary: 'On-device (private)' is the recommended default on capable devices, with a quiet note on which practices suit it — never 'lite/basic'.

title: Pre-launch: App Store AGPL license-grant exception
description:
Before submitting to the iOS App Store, publish a copyright-holder exception that grants Apple the right to distribute the binary under their standard terms.

**Why this is needed**: Apple's App Store Usage Rules (device-count limits, FairPlay DRM, no redistribution) impose restrictions that AGPL §6 forbids ('no further restrictions'). VLC famously got pulled from iOS in 2011 over this exact conflict. The FSF's position is that pure AGPL software cannot legally be distributed via the App Store unless the copyright holder grants an explicit additional permission.

**The fix**: as the copyright holder, add a `LICENSE-EXCEPTION.md` (or equivalent section in README/LICENSE) granting Apple a non-exclusive license to distribute under their terms — AGPL still applies to the source.

Example wording (adjust with legal review):
> The copyright holder additionally grants Apple, Inc. and any party operating under its terms a non-exclusive permission to distribute, link, and combine this software with Apple proprietary frameworks under Apple's standard App Store distribution terms, notwithstanding the restrictions of AGPL §6.

**Contributor caveat**: this only works cleanly if the user is sole copyright holder. Once external contributors gain copyright, they'd need to agree too — easiest pre-launch fix is to add a CONTRIBUTING.md note that submitting code is acknowledgment of the App Store exception, before accepting non-trivial PRs.

Google Play has no equivalent restriction, so this is iOS-only.

Spawned from 2026-05-09 license review. Should land before any App Store submission (related: meditation-pal-7rh).

title: Session-start TTS echo transcribed as phantom user turn

One echo frame at 0.016 RMS tripped speechStarted, which prepended the 2s pre-buffer full of greeting echo. The minSpeechDurationMs guard (speech=0ms!) was then bypassed because the speculative pass returned non-empty text and emittedPartial forces finalization. Fix ideas: (a) raise the echoGate seed/margin so the gate starts above the static floor during TTS, (b) require N consecutive frames above threshold to set speechStarted (single-frame trigger is fragile), (c) don't let emittedPartial override the guard when speechDur is ~0 and ttsActive was set for the whole window. title: Tauri build/release workflow — replace PyInstaller jobs for mac/win/linux
description:
Wire the Tauri shell into release so cutting a release ships the Rust/TS
app instead of the Python/PyInstaller frozen builds. Today release.sh →
build.yml runs PyInstaller for all three platforms; npm run tauri:build
works locally but isn't on any release path.

## Scope

1. **CI workflow** — either replace the macOS/Windows/Linux jobs in
   .github/workflows/build.yml or add a sibling tauri-release.yml.
   Each job runs `npm run tauri:build` after `npm ci` and the Tauri
   prereqs (Rust toolchain, cmake, C compiler for whisper-rs/espeak-rs).
   Upload the produced artifacts to the GH release like the current
   PyInstaller jobs do.

2. **macOS**: adapt the existing cert-import + notarytool keychain
   flow in build.yml (it already imports MACOS_CERTIFICATE +
   MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PWD, stores `notary` credentials). Tauri's bundler
   supports signing + notarization via env vars (APPLE_CERTIFICATE,
   APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY, APPLE_ID, APPLE_PASSWORD, APPLE_TEAM_ID).
   Produces aloud-X.Y.Z-macOS.dmg.

3. **Windows**: Tauri produces MSI + NSIS installers. Decide which (or
   both). Code signing: the Python build is currently unsigned on
   Windows; if we want to sign, plumb a Windows cert via secrets.

4. **Linux**: Tauri produces .deb and AppImage. Match the current
   convention (AppImage) and the file naming
   (aloud-X.Y.Z-Linux.AppImage).

5. **release.sh**: today it reads `__version__` from src/__init__.py
   and lints Python with ruff. Move the version source to
   ts/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json (or ts/package.json) and lint TS+Rust
   instead (npm run typecheck + cargo check, plus cargo deny check).
   Keep the same UX (`scripts/release.sh patch|minor|major|X.Y.Z`).

6. **scripts/build-dmg.sh** — retire once the macOS GH job uses the
   Tauri bundler directly. Until then keep it as a fallback.

## Decision points (call these out in the PR)

- Replace PyInstaller jobs outright vs ship both for one cycle. Recommend
  replace outright once meditation-pal-sk8 lands (Python deletion); until
  then we could run both in parallel to validate.
- Bundler choice on Windows (MSI vs NSIS vs both).
- Whether to add Linux .deb alongside AppImage.

## Acceptance

- A fresh release (test branch or `redo`) produces three signed,
  notarized-where-applicable artifacts:
  - aloud-X.Y.Z-macOS.dmg (signed + notarized)
  - aloud-X.Y.Z-Windows.exe (or .msi)
  - aloud-X.Y.Z-Linux.AppImage
- Each artifact launches and the embedded Rust backend serves /api/*
  (verified via dev-docs/desktop.md's endpoint list).
- The PyInstaller path can be removed without losing release coverage.

## References

- Existing PyInstaller flow: .github/workflows/build.yml, scripts/build-dmg.sh
- Tauri shell: ts/src-tauri/, ts/package.json (tauri:build), dev-docs/desktop.md
- Build prereqs (cmake + C compiler + ort onnxruntime download): see
  dev-docs/desktop.md "Build prerequisites"
- Migration position: meditation-pal-sk8 (Python deletion) should land
  after this so release.sh can be flipped to Tauri only.

- macOS: ggml (whisper.cpp via whisper-rs-sys 0.15) used std::filesystem, which libc++ marks unavailable below macOS 10.15; the build defaulted to 10.13 (Tauri's default minimumSystemVersion) so modern clang (21) hard-errored on <filesystem>. Fix: set minimumSystemVersion '11.0' in tauri.conf.json + MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=11.0 in ts/src-tauri/.cargo/config.toml (covers bare cargo too). VERIFIED locally on clang 21: clean whisper-rs-sys release build finishes clean.
- Linux: onnxruntime prebuilt (ort/piper-rs) references C23 glibc symbols (__isoc23_*, glibc >=2.38); job ran on ubuntu-22.04 (2.35) → rust-lld undefined symbol. Fix: bump to ubuntu-24.04. title: Mobile pricing & monetization spec
description:
Lock in the pricing structure for the standalone mobile app. Goals: accessible price, sustainable economics, no values compromise (no 'pay monthly to feel calm' framing).

Proposed structure (from 2026-05-09 design conversation):
- **App purchase**: ~$7.99 one-time ($5 instinct adjusted for inflation; below $9.99 'real app' threshold but above 'trinket' $4.99)
- **On-device LLM**: free, full functionality, indefinite — the real default
- **BYOK**: free tier, user's own Anthropic/OpenAI/OpenRouter key
- **Hosted cloud**: optional upgrade
  - Pack: ~$4.99 / ~100 sessions (one-time, no recurring)
  - Subscription: ~$3.99/month unlimited (framed as 'we host the model for you', not 'meditation premium')
- **Welcome credit**: app purchase includes a small batch (e.g. 10) of cloud sessions to try the high-quality tier — onboarding hook without subscription pressure

Open math problem:
- Sonnet at ~$0.05–0.20 per 30-min session can underwater the $3.99/mo tier for daily users (30 sessions × $0.20 = $6 cost > $3.99 revenue). Solutions: cheaper default model on the hosted tier (Haiku / Sonnet small / open-weights on a cheap inference provider), soft monthly cap, or reprice.
- Apple/Google take 30% (15% for small business). Net economics need to work after that cut.

Deliverable: a spreadsheet covering median + heavy-user economics, final price points, and an honest copy spec for how the tiers are presented in-app and on the marketing page.

Related: dbd (cloud LLM architecture), toz (web page that may communicate pricing).

Cost lever (added 2026-05-25 by Claude): prompt caching materially changes the per-session math above. The system prompt is currently cached at the default 5-min ephemeral TTL, but sessions have long silent gaps (the 300s check-in is a canned phrase, not an LLM call), so the cache frequently expires between turns and each call repays a ~1.25x cache write instead of a ~0.1x read. A 1h (or adaptive) TTL keeps the prefix warm across pauses and lowers hosted-tier cost. See meditation-pal-ttl for analysis and options. Note: only the direct Anthropic API path can set TTL — the claude-proxy/CLI subscription path cannot.

description:
Today the hosted billing allowlist (ts/server/src/pricing/providers.ts MODELS) pins exact model IDs — opus/sonnet/haiku + gemini-2.5-flash-lite — and surfaces them via GET /cloud/v1/me/models (model-picker.ts 'aloud' branch). Bumping a model = a code edit + release (just did claude-opus-4-7 -> claude-opus-4-8 by hand).

Goal (per user): aloud should pick up the newest model in each family we choose to use WITHOUT an app/server release — fetch live.

Design sketch:
- Define the *families* we offer (anthropic: opus/sonnet/haiku; google: gemini-flash) as patterns/prefixes, not exact IDs.
- Server-side periodic/cached fetch of each provider's model list (Anthropic GET /v1/models already wired in ts/server/src/providers/models.ts; Google has a models endpoint too). Pick the newest matching each family.
- Resolve pricing by FAMILY (a price tier), not exact ID, since the provider model-list endpoints don't return pricing and we can't hand-edit a rate for a model we adopt automatically. meter.ts/providers.ts would key rates on family.
- Keep isModelAllowed() gating: a client may only bill against a family-resolved current model, so it can't invoke an arbitrary expensive model on a user's credits (meditation-pal-8sj).
- Cache + graceful fallback to a pinned default if the list fetch fails (don't break billing if Anthropic's endpoint is down).

OPEN QUESTION / TRADEOFF: providers.ts deliberately keeps prices as one-line, in-the-open diffs precisely so a price change is never a mystery. Auto-adopting a new model means auto-adopting whatever it costs at the family rate — if a new Opus ships at a higher price, we'd under-bill until the family rate is updated. Need user sign-off on family-rate billing before building. Until then, manual bumps (like opus-4-8) are the stopgap.

comments.author: akrusz
comments.text:
User decision: family-rate billing is fine for now (rates within a family rarely vary). Longer-term ask: a server-side service that checks prices DAILY and auto-updates the rate table.

Feasibility — yes. Constraint: no first-party machine-readable pricing API (Anthropic/OpenAI/Google /v1/models return IDs, not prices). Sources that DO work:
  - OpenRouter GET /api/v1/models — per-token prompt/completion prices as JSON, covers Anthropic/Google/OpenAI (proxied), no key.
  - LiteLLM model_prices_and_context_window.json — community-maintained, near-universal coverage, single fetch + diff.

Design (longer-term phase, after the family-rate refactor lands):
  1. Daily cron job in the server software fetches a pricing source.
  2. Extract rates for our families, write to a cached table that meter.ts/providers.ts read instead of hardcoded constants.
  3. Guardrails: only auto-apply within a sane delta (e.g. +/-25%); on a larger jump keep the old rate and ALERT rather than silently re-pricing credits; fall back to pinned defaults if the fetch fails/returns garbage. Retail markup multiplier stays hand-controlled and separate.

This gives auto-updating cost basis with a tripwire against bad upstream numbers mis-billing users.

title: Replace ci.yml Python CI with a TS CI gate (typecheck + vitest + server + cargo check)
description:
GAP found 2026-06-06: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs Python-ONLY on every push/PR — 'ruff check src/ tests/' + 'pytest tests/' — and there is NO TS CI on GitHub Actions. The actual product (ts/) has no CI gate: typecheck, vitest (ui+core), the server's vitest suite, and 'cargo check' for src-tauri only run locally. Two problems: (1) TS regressions aren't caught in CI today; (2) at the ts-core->main merge + Python deletion (sk8), ci.yml would lint/test deleted code and turn main red immediately.

SCOPE: rewrite ci.yml to a Node + (optionally Rust) job: npm ci; npm run typecheck; npm test (root vitest, 243 cases); cd server && npm run typecheck && npm test (268 cases); optionally cargo check -p (src-tauri) behind the Tauri build prereqs. Drop setup-python/portaudio/ruff/pytest steps. Keep on:[push, pull_request]. NOTE the 2 pre-existing failing billing tests (cloud-billing.test.ts) — fix or quarantine before making the suite a required gate, else CI is red from the start.

SEQUENCING: land this WITH or just before sk8 (delete Python) so the swap is atomic — main never has Python CI pointed at deleted code. Pairs with 9vh (which already moved release linting to TS/Rust).
notes: 2026-06-06 IMPLEMENTED. .github/workflows/ci.yml replaced: Python ruff+pytest → TS gate (Node 20, working-directory ts/): npm ci (installs root + @aloud/server workspace from one lockfile) → typecheck → npm test (243 UI/core) → ui:build → server typecheck + test (271) via --workspace. Rust intentionally NOT gated here (needs the full native toolchain; covered by tauri-release.yml). PREREQ DONE: the 2 pre-existing cloud-billing.test.ts failures fixed (stale tests — fetchPacks returns BillingPacks {packs,x402}, startCheckout takes {packId}); suite now fully green (243). Every CI command verified locally. NEEDS first real Actions run to confirm npm ci/setup-node/cache mechanics on the runner. NOTE for the cutover (hpla): for pull_request events GitHub uses the workflow from the BASE branch, so the Python→TS CI swap fully takes effect for PRs only once this lands on main at merge.

title: Adaptive local context management (latency-triggered, invisible) — preserve long-arc continuity
description:
FUTURE / THEORETICAL — do not pull unless latency is actually observed. Split out from meditation-pal-77f so the P1 caching win stays clean.

Worry: with FULL context, a long session re-sends the entire transcript each turn, so a local model (e.g. Gemma 4 26B on a MacBook) re-processes a growing prompt and response latency could climb as the session deepens. NOTE (2026-05-24): the dev reports no meaningful latency on local sessions so far — this is precautionary, not a live problem.

Idea (the dev's framing): build it in as an INVISIBLE, local-only adaptive check — measure per-turn latency, and only if it crosses a threshold, start managing context (e.g. begin summarizing the oldest turns into a running synopsis) so responses stay snappy. Stay dormant/no-op otherwise.

HARD CONSTRAINT: long-arc continuity is load-bearing for exploration quality — a good session calls back to material from 30+ min earlier ('the balance from earlier', 'little Alex'). Any trimming MUST preserve that (running summary of trimmed turns, not a naive rolling window). This is a quality-sensitive design task, unlike the caching ticket which is quality-neutral.

Applies to all paths but motivated by local. Companion to meditation-pal-77f.

title: Voice command 'mute' (and hold-family) not parsed in TS

TS has no transcript-level command parsing anywhere — every final goes to respondTo as a literal turn. Note: TS button tooltips do NOT over-promise these (verified), so it's a lost affordance, not a broken promise. Found by post-sk8 parity sweep.

title: Add cheaper TTS provider/voice tiers (TTS is the dominant cost line)
description:
TTS is the DOMINANT provider-cost line for a session, so a cheaper voice tier is the single biggest margin/credit-burn lever. Modeled 30-min session (90 cycles, one human + one AI sentence per ~20s), verified against the live priceSession():
  - Opus:   LLM $0.249 + STT $0.007 + TTS $0.297 = $0.553  (~11.0 cr, ~$1.38 retail)
  - Gemini: LLM $0.005 + STT $0.007 + TTS $0.297 = $0.308  (~6.2 cr,  ~$0.77 retail)
TTS at ~$0.30 is 54% of the Opus session and ~96% of the Gemini session. Halving TTS roughly halves a value-tier session's cost.

Context: the live backend is Google Chirp3-HD ($30/1M). The meter now bills by actual Google voice tier (googleTtsRateFor, providers.ts), so moving to a cheaper Google tier needs NO new integration — just adding voices to CURATED_VOICES (voice-catalog.ts). A non-Google provider needs (a) a synth adapter alongside synthesizeWithGoogle, and (b) a rate entry in the meter (generalize the TTS pricer to be provider-aware, not just Google-tier-aware).

SCOPE / DECISION:
1. Quick win, zero integration: add Google Neural2 voices ($16/1M = half Chirp3-HD) as a "value voice" tier; audition for calm quality. Possibly make a value voice the DEFAULT to minimize credit burn, keeping Chirp3-HD as a premium pick.
2. Bigger cut: add one non-Google provider from the shortlist (see comment) behind the TTS abstraction.
3. Generalize TTS pricing: ttsRateFor should key off (provider, voice), not assume Google. Each new voice MUST have a verified rate before it can bill.
4. Reconcile estimateVoices()/CURATED_VOICES so the picker + /me/estimates reflect whatever tiers we offer (the unification from the last change makes this one place).

Supersedes the closed meditation-pal-2gz's landscape note (which had Hume at a wrong ~$7.60 — it's actually ~$150 PAYG). Relates to pricing calibration (rvy, 7xl).

comments.author: akrusz
comments.text:
TTS PROVIDER LANDSCAPE — web-verified May/June 2026, per 1M chars, PAYG/API rate, adversarially fact-checked (corrects several widely-circulated wrong figures). All are simple stateless REST (server-held key, no GPU) unless noted.

CHEAPEST CREDIBLE (open-weight, hosted — ~40x cheaper than Chirp3-HD):
  - Kokoro-82M via Replicate ~$0.65 / DeepInfra ~$0.80 / OpenRouter ~$0.62. Topped TTS Arena; pleasant/calm-capable. Tradeoff: smaller voice set, less emotional nuance; audition for "calm" not "neutral". Hosted endpoints keep the stateless/no-GPU model (self-hosting Kokoro would break it).

HALF-OR-LESS of Chirp3-HD, premium-neural quality, drop-in:
  - OpenAI gpt-4o-mini-tts ~$12-15 (effective; token-billed, 2k-token input cap/call). STEERABLE — can be told "speak slowly, softly, long pauses" = ideal meditation fit. TOP PICK.
  - Deepgram Aura-1 $15 ($13.50 Growth). Natural, <90ms latency. Fewer voices.
  - Fish Audio S2 Pro $15 (per UTF-8 byte; commercial rights need paid plan — check license).
  - OpenAI tts-1 $15. Warm, simple, no emotion steering.
  - Google Neural2 $16 / Amazon Polly Neural $16 / Azure Neural ~$15. Same quality class as current, half the price, safest "sounds like what we have" swap. Google Neural2 = zero new integration.

AT/ABOVE current cost — sound great but no savings:
  - Deepgram Aura-2 $30, Amazon Polly Generative $30, Azure Neural HD $22, Rime Mist $30, Cartesia Sonic 3 ~$38-50, Inworld Max $35, ElevenLabs Flash v2.5 $60, ElevenLabs Multilingual v2 $120.

AVOID for cost (common myths corrected):
  - Hume Octave — $150/1M PAYG (only $50/1M at $500/mo Business). The "$7.60/1M" figure in the old 2gz note and around the web is WRONG vs Hume's own pricing page. Conceptually ideal (emotion-directable) but not cheap until high volume.
  - Unreal Speech "$4/1M" — only at 1B+ chars/mo; realistic small-scale ~$12-16 with quality below Google neural. Not the bargain it markets.

RECOMMENDATION: (1) immediate — offer Google Neural2 as a value tier (no integration, half cost); (2) evaluate OpenAI gpt-4o-mini-tts (steerable-calm, ~half cost) and hosted Kokoro (~40x cheaper, audition required) as the two highest-leverage adds. Verify each rate against a real bill before it bills users.

Sources: cloud.google.com/text-to-speech/pricing · aws.amazon.com/polly/pricing · azure.microsoft.com/pricing/details/speech · deepgram.com/pricing · openai.com/api/pricing · elevenlabs.io/pricing/api · hume.ai/pricing · cartesia.ai/pricing · rime.ai/pricing · inworld.ai/pricing · openrouter.ai/hexgrad/kokoro-82m · replicate.com/jaaari/kokoro-82m · deepinfra.com/hexgrad/Kokoro-82M

title: Gift clouds: buy credits for another user by email (accept/decline on sign-in)
description:
Lets user A buy a credit pack as a GIFT to user B by email. Money model (sanity-checked with dev): the Stripe payment clears immediately like a normal purchase; the clouds become a PENDING gift, granted exactly once — to the recipient on accept, or back to the BUYER on decline / 60-day expiry (no Stripe refund). So a rejected gift can never cancel a transaction, double-grant, lose money, or go negative.

Implemented (server): gifts table + store methods (createGift idempotent on stripe session; resolveGift atomic compare-and-set so accept/decline/expire can't double-resolve); credits/gifts.ts (acceptGift/declineGift/reconcileExpiredGifts/pendingGiftsForAccount, GIFT_EXPIRY_SECONDS=60d); billing webhook branches on metadata gift_to_email to record a pending gift instead of crediting the buyer; checkout accepts giftToEmail; routes /cloud/v1/gifts (list/:id/accept/:id/decline); hourly expiry sweep in index.ts. Tests: gifts.test.ts (10) + store parity.

Implemented (UI): buy-credits modal 'For myself / Gift to someone' toggle + recipient email; cloud-billing fetchGifts/acceptGift/declineGift + startCheckout(giftToEmail); gift-modal.ts accept/decline prompt shown at boot + after sign-in. Tests: cloud-billing gifts (4).

Lives on our server (no external email yet). FOLLOW-UPS: email notifications to the recipient ('you've been gifted clouds') and to the buyer on accept/decline/expiry; chargeback edge (buyer disputes after recipient spends) noted on meditation-pal-7tl.

title: Free-tier privacy lockdown: hide live transcript / lock kasina mode / audio-only to deter LLM scraping
description: For sessions on FREE credits, reduce the surface for scraping the LLM's text output at scale. Options (pick/stack): (1) disable the chat bubbles / live transcript display so model text never renders client-side; (2) force kasina mode ON and lock it (minimal-visual, eyes-closed framing) for free sessions; (3) stretch goal — pipe ONLY synthesized audio to the client for free sessions, never the response text, so there's no machine-readable transcript to harvest. Tradeoff: hurts accessibility/UX for legit free users, so gate it to free tier only and revisit if it bites conversion. Low priority — defense-in-depth, not load-bearing. Developer ask 2026-05-31.

With this, all three audio.js niceties (speculative / adaptive silence / pre-buffer) are ported. Remaining before close: hands-on barge-in verification in the Tauri desktop window (user testing).

title: Web demo of aloud. (hosted, accounts + credits)
description:
Umbrella for making aloud. accessible as a hosted web demo (distinct from the marketing page in meditation-pal-toz). A stranger hits a URL, signs in, gets 1-2 free sessions on a cheap/on-device-class model, then buys credits to access premium LLMs and voices, with margin built in.

Key architectural reframe (2026-05-23 design conversation): the web demo is a DEPLOYMENT TARGET of the TS rewrite (meditation-pal-2qg), not a separate build. The ts/ui Vite build (ui/dist) is static and can sit on the existing static host (e.g. GitHub Pages); only a backend proxy needs a server. The web STT/TTS/LLM adapters already exist under ts/ui/src/adapters (web-speech-stt, server-whisper-stt, server-tts, claude-proxy-http) but currently point at the desktop Flask backend — the web demo must decouple them onto a standalone hosted backend.

Relationship to mobile plans: this REUSES meditation-pal-dbd (cloud LLM proxy) and meditation-pal-a2j (pricing/monetization). The web variant differs from mobile in three ways worth a fresh spec: (1) no 30% app-store tax — Stripe ~3%, roughly doubling margin headroom and softening a2j's cost-math trap; (2) auth is web OAuth (Google/Apple/etc.) not IAP; (3) abuse surface is wide open (no app-store gating), so free-tier quota/abuse controls are load-bearing.

Blocked by the TS rewrite reaching browser-usable parity (meditation-pal-2qg).
notes: ARCH DECISION (2026-05-24, with developer): the server lives in the SAME public AGPL repo as a workspace package (ts/server, @aloud/server), NOT a separate/private repo. Rationale: developer wants the server open source too (privacy + ownership values; meditation app). Once open, AGPL flips from liability to asset — its network-use clause guarantees the deployed server stays open. The only arguably-sensitive value, the margin multiplier, is intentionally PUBLISHED (GET /v1/me/models). Non-disruptive workspace layout chosen to run in parallel with the TS conversion: ts/src and ts/ui were NOT moved; ts/package.json gained a 'workspaces' field; the full packages/{core,ui,server} rename is deferred to a coordinated step later. Scaffold landed on branch ts-server (see ts/server/README.md). Next session: do NOT default to a private repo or to scaffolding from scratch.

title: Hosted pass-through abuse & cost controls (web-first)
description:
Cost-control + abuse-mitigation for the free hosted pass-through (LLM/TTS/STT) so account-farming or a viral/scripted spike can't produce an unbounded bill. Web-first: the strong mobile primitives (App Store receipt, App Attest, Play Integrity) don't exist in the browser — on web you only have leaky identifiers (IP, cookie, OAuth, CAPTCHA), so identity can't be the safety boundary. Build the defense around bounded pools + money instead.

Business-model context (2026-05-27): app, website, and desktop program are ALL free. Revenue is donations + an optional paid pass-through for people who want us to conveniently host LLM/TTS/STT. New accounts get a fixed one-time batch of free credits (all they ever get free); users can buy more. Average cost/session is shown up front so a user knows before starting whether they need to top up.

Two distinct abuse vectors:
1. Volume / farming — one person making new accounts to reset the free credit grant.
2. Repurposing — scripting our endpoints as a free general-purpose LLM/TTS/STT API. This is the vector most likely to actually cost real money, and it's independent of identity.

Controls, in priority order:
- **Systemwide daily budget cap (hard backstop).** A ceiling on total free spend/credits per day across all users, per service. Bounds the worst case absolutely regardless of how many accounts are farmed — this is what makes imperfect Sybil resistance acceptable. UX: check at session START; if the daily free pool is exhausted, don't start NEW free sessions, but let any in-flight session finish (never cut someone off mid-meditation). Implies a start-time cost estimate / reservation.
- **Resume / continue-from-history counts as a session START.** Resuming a past session (the continue-from-history flow: history.ts sets sessionStorage 'continueFrom' → session.ts loadExchanges) must pass the same daily-cap + credit check and reserve estimated cost up front, exactly like a fresh session. The 'let in-flight sessions finish' carve-out applies ONLY to a session already actively running — NEVER to resuming a historical one, or it's a trivial bypass (sit over the cap, resume an old session, keep spending free). Resume replays the prior transcript as context, so its first request is often LARGER/costlier than a fresh start — estimate on the actual replayed payload, not a flat per-session figure.
- **Constrain the proxy server-side (kills vector 2).** Accept only the structured meditation request and assemble the real provider call server-side — fixed/whitelisted system prompt, capped max_tokens, the app's own message shape; never forward arbitrary request bodies. Same for TTS/STT (cap input length, no arbitrary params). Highest-value control, needs no identity. (See the open-relay note from the ts-core review: src/web/llm_proxy.py currently forwards bodies unchanged.)
- **Per-account free credit grant (a monetary balance, not a fixed session count).** One-time batch on signup; depletes with use; buy-more to continue. Users pick ANY model, with transparent per-model cost shown before a session begins — so the same grant might buy ~1 Opus session or ~10 Gemini Flash sessions. Start-time estimates, credit deduction, and daily-cap accounting are all denominated in money at the CHOSEN model's rate (a cheap default is fine, but it's a default, not a restriction).
- **Light per-client friction.** IP + cookie rate limits; a bot challenge (e.g. Cloudflare Turnstile) on web. On mobile, optionally use device attestation (App Attest / Play Integrity) for a cleaner per-device identity + a more generous cap — a bonus, not the web baseline.
- **BYOK + on-device as the always-free escape hatch.** Every client can run the user's own key or an on-device model, so hitting the free cap never blocks a real user — they switch and keep going. This is what lets us cap the free pool aggressively without harming legit users.
- **Cheap default model on the free hosted tier** (e.g. Haiku, not Sonnet) to lower the abuse ceiling and stretch the daily pool. (Ties to the cost-math TODO in dbd / a2j.)

Why NOT 'sign in with Google/Apple' as the limiter: Google accounts are free to mint, so federated sign-in barely raises farming cost while adding friction and excluding accountless / iPhone-on-web users. Identity is at most a secondary fairness tool (per-user daily share), never the boundary.

All of this lives on the hosted backend (see dbd); some pieces (attestation, receipt checks) require real-device testing. Decisions here are small and align with the existing pricing direction; the architecture supports staying fully free (cap + fallback) or layering an optional paid 'higher/unmetered cap' tier later without re-architecting.

title: API key UX: Get-key link + paste-from-clipboard for all providers

title: Desktop updater: tauri-plugin-updater + signing keypair

title: Cross-platform credits: sell on web (Stripe), spend on mobile — bypass IAP cut
description:
STRATEGY + SPEC. Make credits a portable account-bound currency so users can BUY them on the web store (Stripe, ~3-5% all-in) and SPEND them in the mobile app — instead of buying via Apple/Google IAP and losing 15-30%. This is the 'Pokemon Go / Fortnite web store' model and is potentially the single biggest lever on the economics meditation-pal-a2j worries about (a2j assumes a 30% store tax that this largely removes).

Why it's newly viable (verified 2026-05, but UNSETTLED — re-check before building):
- US: since the Apr/May-2025 Epic v. Apple contempt ruling, App Store apps may link out to external web purchases with NO Apple commission and no entitlement. Dec-2025 Ninth Circuit largely upheld this.
- RISK: the Ninth Circuit said Apple MAY set a 'reasonable commission' on externally-linked purchases; the framework is still being decided on remand and Apple is seeking Supreme Court review (rehearing denied Mar-2026, remand proceeding Apr-2026). So US ~0% commission is real today but could change.
- EU: NOT free — External Purchase Link entitlement required and Core Technology Commission (~12-20%) applies. Model EU separately.
- You take on payment processing, sales tax/VAT, fraud, and compliance for web-sold credits.

Design notes:
- Credits must be account-bound (requires the OAuth/account model, meditation-pal-rfb) and balance-checked server-side by the proxy so they're spendable cross-device.
- The mobile app links out to the web checkout (compliant external link), user returns and balance reflects the top-up.
- Keep an IAP path as fallback for users who won't leave the app / for jurisdictions where external links are restricted; accept the cut there.

Depends on the credits/billing engine (meditation-pal-8sj) and accounts (meditation-pal-rfb). Extends meditation-pal-a2j. Child of the web demo epic; serves mobile economics.

title: Cloud LLM proxy for standalone mobile
description:
Server-side LLM access for the standalone mobile app, structured as a tiered offering rather than a single proxy.

Tiers (per 2026-05-09 design conversation):
- **Free / on-device**: small LLM running locally (Apple Intelligence Foundation Models on iOS 18+, Gemma/Phi/Llama 3.2 via MLC-LLM or llama.cpp on Android). Always available, no network, full privacy. Default mode.
- **BYOK**: user supplies their own Anthropic/OpenAI/OpenRouter key. Free tier — power users who want best quality at their own cost.
- **Hosted cloud**: paid access to a curated high-quality model. Two purchase shapes:
  - Session pack: ~$4.99 for ~100 sessions (one-time, no recurring)
  - Subscription: ~$3.99/month unlimited (clearly framed as paying for compute, not for meditation content)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Cost math: Sonnet at ~$0.05–0.20 per 30-min session could underwater the $3.99/mo tier for heavy users. Either choose a cheaper default model (Haiku, Sonnet 4 small, etc.), put a soft cap, or reprice. Needs spreadsheet pass before commit.
- Hosted backend stack — keep Python Flask, or rewrite in TypeScript so the mobile + desktop stories converge? See separate decision ticket.
- Abuse / quota / auth model for hosted tier (per-user keys, sign-in with Apple/Google).
- Transparency copy: ensure the on-device tier is honestly framed as 'real and complete', not crippleware.

Phase 1 (phone-as-remote, jim) doesn't need any of this — it talks to the user's own desktop. This ticket is for Phase 2 (standalone install).

Cost lever (added 2026-05-25 by Claude): prompt-cache TTL is a direct knob on the hosted-tier cost math above. The default 5-min ephemeral cache on the system prompt dies during meditation's long silent gaps, so calls repay cache writes (~1.25x) rather than reads (~0.1x). A 1h or adaptive TTL keeps the prefix warm. See meditation-pal-ttl. Caveats: TTL control exists only on the direct Anthropic API provider, not the claude-proxy/CLI path; and today only the system prompt is cached (not the growing conversation), so confirm the rendered prompt clears the model's min-cacheable size (~2048 tokens Sonnet 4.6 / 4096 Opus) before relying on it.

**Key correction (2026-05-23): retention is a TOGGLE, and the default DEPENDS on deployment context — do NOT make ephemeral the global default.**
- **Local / single-user (desktop, on-device mobile):** keep session history by DEFAULT — this is the current behavior (sessions auto-save; there's a History view). It's the user's own device; retention is a feature they rely on. Per-session opt-out already exists conceptually as Private Session Mode (meditation-pal-ht8).
- **Multi-user hosted (the web demo / cloud backend):** default to NO server-side retention of transcripts (ephemeral). This is where storing strangers' intimate disclosures is a real risk. Still a toggle — a signed-in user could opt IN to saving their own history server-side if we offer accounts — but off by default.

So: one retention setting, context-aware default (local on / hosted off), surfaced clearly to the user.

**Also in scope:**
- Short, clear privacy statement.
- Per-provider data-flow disclosure: where audio/text actually goes (e.g. Web Speech API ships audio to Google; Groq/Anthropic API retention terms; on-device = nothing leaves the device).
- Tie the "nothing is stored" promise to the privacy-as-positioning angle (see related positioning work) — for hosted, prove it in the UI.

title: Accept payments via x402 (stablecoin/HTTP-402) as a credit purchase channel
description:
Add x402 (the open HTTP-402 "Payment Required" protocol — programmatic USDC payments, primarily on Base L2, settled over HTTP via a facilitator) as a THIRD credit-purchase channel alongside Stripe and IAP.

WHY:
- Cheapest channel by far. Commission ~0% (just gas/facilitator) vs Stripe ~2.9%+30c and Apple/Google IAP 15-30%. Drops straight to margin or lets us lower prices. Fits the existing commission model (pricing/commission.ts): add channel 'x402' at ~0% — assertSolvent clears it trivially.
- Agent-native. x402 is built for machine/agent payments (pay-per-request). aloud is an AI app; an agent could autonomously top up credits. No card, no account, no redirect.
- On-chain settlement = no chargebacks.

HOW IT FITS (the credit system is already channel-agnostic):
- New PurchaseChannel 'x402' in contract.ts + a ~0 entry in commission.ts.
- Billing route: client requests a pack → server responds 402 with payment requirements (USDC amount, recipient address, facilitator, nonce) → client pays → server verifies settlement via the facilitator → ledger.purchase(credits). Same terminal step as the Stripe webhook, different proof.
- Pricing unchanged: USDC ~= USD, so the ☁️ / credit / $ model and pack prices stay as-is.
- Pack purchase fits best; true per-request 402 metering is a possible later mode.

OPEN QUESTIONS / RISKS:
- Treasury & custody: a wallet to receive USDC on Base; off-ramp to fiat (providers bill us in USD), FX/treasury ops. Self-custody vs Coinbase.
- Facilitator: Coinbase's hosted x402 facilitator (verify+settle) vs self-hosted.
- Compliance: crypto acceptance has per-jurisdiction AML/KYC + tax implications. Stripe Tax handled sales tax/VAT; x402 does not — figure out tax collection.
- Refunds: on-chain is final → need a manual refund path.
- Scope a thin MVP: pack purchase via Base USDC + Coinbase facilitator + manual off-ramp; gate behind a flag.

Depends on the credits/billing backend (8sj). Relates to the commission/solvency model and the gift flow (same ledger.purchase terminal). Queued by dev to do next alongside 6lt.

title: NEDERA: Differentiate 5-level feeling-word corpus + resonance prompting (craft-heavy)
description:
The hardest content problem in the mode. Part of epic meditation-pal-pmxb.

The Differentiate stage needs Tataryn's 5-level taxonomy baked into the prompts with real vocabulary, so the facilitator can offer **precise candidate feeling words** (the blog hammers that *specificity = resonance* — "I feel alone" lands where "I feel sad" doesn't).

## The 5 levels (most intellectual -> most somatic)
1. **Situations** — the story, intellectually ("she criticized my work").
2. **Emotions** — the 4 primary: happiness, sadness, anger, fear.
3. **Interpersonal feelings** — relational, the "-ed" words: betrayed, abandoned, valued, dismissed.
4. **Core feelings** — 9 polarity pairs about self-identity: alone/connected, bad/good, powerless/empowered, etc. (the recurring "hotspots").
5. **Feeling-beliefs** — the deepest layer, simple convictions: "nobody will ever love me," "I'm fundamentally flawed" (schemas / samskaras).

## Build
- Encode each level with vocabulary + strong few-shot examples (instructions alone won't get specificity — the model defaults to generic mush).
- Resonance-check prompting: facilitator offers a phrase -> user repeats aloud -> **pause (reuse [HOLD]/silence)** -> user reports body response (voice change, tears, shift, or nothing) -> if it doesn't land, revise and try again.
- A small classifier ("did that resonate?") modeled on `ts/src/facilitation/resume-intent.ts`.

## Caution
- Specificity must stay *offered*, never *imposed* — the user confirms what's true in their body; the facilitator never declares their feeling for them.

title: Resume-intent classifier traps user in hold on provider error (429/5xx) — no voice escape
description: When the facilitator is in silence/hold mode, the ONLY voice exit is classifyResumeIntent (resume-intent.ts), an LLM call. Its catch returns false ('stay in the hold') for ANY error — including provider failures (429 quota, 5xx, timeout), not just a genuine 'not ready to resume.' Observed in the wild: aloud cloud session on gemini-2.5-flash-lite hit 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, so every resume attempt threw -> returned false -> the meditator could not leave the hold by voice at all (dead session). Two fixes: (1) distinguish a provider/transport error from a clean 'NO' verdict — on a hard error, fail toward escape (resume) or surface a recoverable error, rather than silently trapping; (2) treat substantive on-topic speech as implicit resume so a MISTAKEN hold self-corrects, not only literal 'let's continue.' See handleSilenceUtterance in ui/src/views/session.ts. Compounds with the HOLD-on-fragment misfire bead.

title: Device-independent VAD: ratio-based thresholds or Silero
description: All quiet-side VAD gates in ui/src/adapters/whisper-pcm-stt.ts are absolute RMS constants tuned on the dev MBP (energyThreshold 0.015, BARGE_IN_THRESHOLD 0.03, echo/noise seeds 0.005). noiseFloor*3 adapts the gate UP for noisy rooms but nothing ever adapts DOWN for quiet mics - on low-level hardware soft speech sits under 0.015 permanently (constant mid-sentence cutoffs) or speech never trips the gate. Web Safari/Firefox + cloud-STT users hit this same adapter with different AGC behavior underneath. Step 1 (keeps architecture): track a speech-level EMA over confirmed-speech frames and derive gates as ratios of it (e.g. release ~10% of speech level, floored at noiseFloor*k) so tuning transfers across devices. Step 2 (robust): replace RMS gating with Silero VAD (MIT, ~1MB ONNX, onnxruntime-web/WASM, 16kHz, per-30ms speech probability) - handles soft speech vs breath and device variance outright, and gives the incompleteness-aware end-of-turn bead a trustworthy speech signal to build on. title: NEDERA: stage state machine + transition signaling (ts/src/facilitation/nedera.ts)
description:
Core orchestration for the NEDERA mode — the stage state machine, parallel to how `noting` got its own module rather than bending `exploration`. Part of epic meditation-pal-pmxb.

## Build
- New module `ts/src/facilitation/nedera.ts`: `Stage` enum (Notice, Experience, Differentiate, Express, Resonate, Resolve, TakeAction/Update), a `NederaController` holding `currentStage`, building the per-stage system prompt, and deciding transitions.
- **Non-linear movement:** Resonate must be able to loop back to Differentiate; any stage can drop to a paused/grounding state (see SAFETY child).
- **Transition signaling:** LLM emits a control prefix parsed the same way as `parseHoldSignal()` in `ts/src/facilitation/prompts.ts` (e.g. `[ADVANCE]` / `[BACK]`). Add a `parseStageSignal()` alongside it.
- **Bias conservative:** a false advance that rushes someone past an unfelt emotion is the core failure mode. Require corroboration (user report + model signal) before advancing; default to staying.

## Reuse
- Mirror the structure of the `noting` orchestration (its own session path) rather than overloading `PromptBuilder`.
- Inherit base voice fragments (warm, no emojis, no filler) from `prompts.ts` for tonal consistency.

Depends on SAFETY child (resistance/pause states are part of the machine).

title: Loopback Whisper relay: free local STT for non-Chrome browsers
description:
Give browsers without the Web Speech API (Firefox, etc.) a free, local STT path instead of forcing aloud cloud (metered) — by making the desktop's local Whisper reachable from a same-machine browser.

Key insight: the browser mic already works — getUserMedia is fine at localhost (secure context), and CloudWhisperSttEngine already captures PCM + POSTs to a whisper endpoint. The only missing piece for Firefox is a *reachable* whisper endpoint; it doesn't need a new capture path.

Approach (most valuable first):
1. Expose the Tauri Rust shell's /app/v1/stt/whisper to a same-machine browser. Today it's on a dynamic loopback port reachable only by the embedded webview (injected base). Needs: a known/discoverable port (currently dynamic), CORS for the browser origin, and (in dev) the Vite proxy forwarding /app/v1/stt/whisper to that port instead of Hono. Payoff: free + private local Whisper in any browser on the machine, while the desktop app is running.
2. Self-hosted Hono with a server-side whisper (whisper.cpp) — a relay for people running their own server.
3. aloud cloud STT already IS the relay for the hosted product (metered, needs sign-in) — so the gap is only the free/local path.

Risks/cost: dynamic loopback port discovery; CORS; only works while the desktop app runs; loopback-only (127.0.0.1) keeps it on-machine — a LAN variant reopens the security questions that got 8zj removed and overlaps with jim (PWA phone-as-remote).

Context: current behavior gates 'Whisper (on this device)' on isTauri() (stt-picker.ts), so browsers default to web-speech (Chrome) or aloud cloud. This bead is the free path for the rest.

title: Cloud STT endpointing: dangling-clause guard loses race to silence window, cuts mid-sentence
description: On the WhisperPcmSttEngine cloud path (Firefox/Safari + aloud cloud), the meditator gets cut off mid-sentence. The incomplete-clause protection (INCOMPLETE_CLAUSE_EXTRA_MS, bead fxo1) only arms AFTER a speculative transcription round-trips to the cloud and sets this.partialIncomplete (whisper-pcm-stt.ts, start() poll loop). But the audio callback (handleAudio) independently finalizes the turn once silence >= needed, where needed includes the +4000ms extra ONLY if partialIncomplete is already true. On the cloud path the round-trip (1-3s, grows with buffer) can lose the race to the base silence window (silenceBaseMs 3000ms floor), so the turn submits with partialIncomplete=false and the dangling-clause result is dropped (the !this.utteranceDone guard). Repro transcripts ended on 'an element of' / 'feeling of' (textbook DANGLING_TAIL_WORDS). On desktop Whisper the spec pass is local+instant so it always wins — cloud-only bug. Fix: don't finalize while a speculative pass is in flight (hoist specInFlight to an instance field, gate the utteranceDone branch on it) so the latest dangling verdict is always applied before submit. Keep the maxUtterance runaway valve unguarded. Relates fxo1.

title: Idea: multi-state orb (listening/thinking/speaking/holding visual modes)

During the TS rewrite I prototyped a session orb with distinct visual modes for each conversation phase, then reverted to the existing app's breathing/holding states under the lift-first rule (see meditation-pal-cfy). User liked the idea and wants to revisit after parity work is done.

The prototype had:
- orb-listening: hue-rotate(-20deg), saturate(1.2), 1.4s pulse animation (transform + box-shadow grow)
- orb-thinking: saturate(0.5), 1.2s contracting pulse (subtle inhale)
- orb-speaking: brightness(1.15), 0.9s 3-keyframe ripple
- orb-holding: existing app's silence mode, but slower 9s breathe

Driven by setOrb(mode) calls in session.ts at:
- start of LLM thinking: setOrb('thinking')
- start of TTS playback: setOrb('speaking')
- HOLD signal received: setOrb('holding')
- mic active: setOrb('listening')
- idle: setOrb('idle') -> orb-breathing

Decision needed: do these augment the existing orb states (orb-breathing + orb-holding + orb-muted + orb-kasina + orb-rainbow), replace any, or live as their own mode set the user can opt into?

Original implementation lives in commit 1c14861 (later reverted in 29fc6d8) for reference.

title: Pre-launch: protect the 'aloud.' brand (stylized mark, weak-word strategy)
description:
Protect the "aloud." brand before App Store launch. Name is FINAL (2026-05-23) — see context below; this ticket is about HOW to protect a deliberately-chosen weak word, not whether to reconsider it.

**Context / decisions:**
- The old name "glooow" and anything "glow"-adjacent is permanently dead: the meditation app GLO holds and actively enforces a trademark against similar-sounding names. Not a taste call — a legal one.
- "aloud." was chosen knowing it's a common dictionary word with weaker enforceability (descriptive for a voice app; likely descriptiveness refusal on the bare word). The user has explored alternatives; everything good is overloaded/taken. Decision stands.
- The moat is therefore TRUST + PRIVACY + PROMPT CRAFT, not brand-law. Trademark is defensive hygiene, not the strategy.

**Approach (given the weak word):**
- Pursue a STYLIZED wordmark / logo / composite mark (design + word) rather than the bare word "aloud" — stylization adds the distinctiveness the bare word lacks and is far more registrable.
- USPTO search in class 9 (software) + class 41 (services); expect to need the stylized mark to clear.
- File via TEAS (~$250-350); a TM attorney ($500-1500) is more clearly worth it here given descriptiveness risk — get a quick read on the stylized-mark path before filing.
- Common-law use protects the styled brand automatically to a degree; registration of the stylized mark is what enables App Store clone takedowns.
- Defer international (Madrid) until traction.

title: Cloud STT bills speculative passes - 2-3x effective rate vs displayed
description: Server bills every /cloud/v1/stt request by audio-seconds (routes/stt.ts debit 'stt:provider:Xs'). The whisper-pcm engine's speculative transcription (live preview during pauses) re-sends the ENTIRE growing utterance buffer on each pause >500ms, so a 20s turn with 2 pauses bills ~2-3x its actual speech duration for hosted-STT users. Compounding: (1) the client-side session tally counts only the final pass (whisper-pcm-stt.ts comment says 'revisit if a hosted cloud-STT meters speculation' - it does), so in-app usage understates the real debit; (2) the incompleteness hold (fxo1) lengthens turns slightly, adding ~1 spec pass. Desktop/local Whisper unaffected. Affects pricing calibration (rvy) - the ~1 credit/hour STT estimate assumes actual speech seconds. Mitigations: throttle spec passes on the billed path (e.g. min 2s of new audio between passes), and/or spec-transcribe only a trailing window (final pass stays full-buffer), and/or count spec seconds into the client tally so the display is honest either way.

comments.author: akrusz
comments.text: Cost math (2026-06-09): STT = $0.054/hr audio (Fireworks v3-turbo); typical session 240s speech = $0.0036 = 0.072 credits (~0.086 cr/hr; displayed '1/hr' is Math.ceil - 11x overstatement). Worst-case 4x speculation multiplier: ~1.4c provider cost/session, ~0.35 cr/hr - still under the displayed rate. NOT worth engineering for cost. Residual value: client tally counts only the final pass (display honesty, pennies), and consider showing 0.1/hr instead of ceil'd 1/hr in the rvy calibration pass.
